column1: Pour 3/4 gallon (2.8 L) of warm water into a clean bucket or cooler. Add the brown sugar, salt, shallots, garlic, peppercorns, juniper and herbs and stir until the salt and sugar dissolve. Let the brine cool completely.

Lower the turkey into the cooled brine and pour in the 3/4 gallon (2.8 L) of cold pineapple juice, adding more cold water if needed to fully submerge it. Use canned or boiled-and-cooled juice; raw fresh pineapple juice will turn the meat mushy.
Keep it cold: cover and refrigerate a bucket, or pack a cooler with ice so it stays at 40°F (4°C) or below.
Brine 12–24 hours. Don't go longer: the acidic pineapple juice will make the outer meat mealy.
Remove the turkey and give it a quick rinse under cold water so the pineapple sugar doesn't scorch. Pat completely dry and refrigerate uncovered on a rack, ideally overnight, so the skin dries out.
Rub the dry skin all over with softened butter. Optionally tuck herbs into the cavity.

Roast at 325°F (163°C) for about 3.5–3.75 hours (about 15 minutes per pound / 33 minutes per kg). Check the skin around the 2-hour mark and tent loosely with foil once it turns deep golden brown, since the pineapple sugars brown quickly. Roast until the thickest part of the breast reaches 165°F (74°C).
Rest at least 25–30 minutes before carving.
